html:
The wars of 58 to 50 BCE in which Julius Caesar conquered Gaul, the land of the Gauls, roughly modern France, Belgium and Switzerland.

Caesar went to Gaul as governor and looked for reasons to fight. The main stages were:

  • 58 BCE: he stopped the Helvetii migration and drove the German king Ariovistus back over the Rhine;
  • 57 to 56 BCE: he beat the Belgae of the north and the seafaring Veneti of Brittany;
  • 55 to 54 BCE: he bridged the Rhine and made the invasions of Britain;
  • 52 BCE: Vercingetorix led a revolt of nearly all Gaul, which ended at the Siege of Alesia;
  • 51 to 50 BCE: he crushed the last resistance.

The cost was huge. Ancient writers claimed a million Gauls died and another million were enslaved; the true numbers are unknown but large. Caesar became enormously rich, and his legions became loyal to him above all.

Gaul became Roman for five centuries, and its people came to speak Latin, the root of French. The war also handed Caesar the army he used in Caesar's civil war. He told the story himself in his Gallic War.
sum: The wars of 58 to 50 BCE in which Julius Caesar conquered Gaul, the land of the Gauls, roughly modern France, Belgium and Switzerland.
